feeds.title: SuperFly Physics
feeds.description: At SuperFly Physics, Andy Rundquist shares ideas for teaching physics, fun science experiments, and interesting physics problems.

feeds.title: The Science Penguin Blog
feeds.description: Covers Science resources for busy upper elementary teachers. Ari Mosquera, the 5th-grade science teacher, created The Science Penguin to share her own science materials, informational texts, simple labs, assessments, and lesson planning guides.

feeds.title: The Tech Savvy Science Teacher
feeds.description: A science teacher shares her journey through technology use in the classroom.

feeds.title: The Trendy Science Teacher Blog
feeds.description: The Trendy Science Teacher blog offers practical ideas for science educators, with a focus on biology, physical science, and forensics classrooms. It features posts on topics like creating an emergency sub binder, fun review games, hands-on labs, and classroom management strategies.

feeds.title: Science Lessons That Rock Blog
feeds.description: The Science Lessons That Rock blog provides tips and resources for teaching science. It covers a wide range of subjects, including lesson plans for earthquakes, decomposers, DNA structure, and atmosphere.

feeds.title: The Learning Scientists Blog
feeds.description: We are cognitive psychological scientists interested in research on education. Our main research focus is on the science of learning. Our vision is to make scientific research on learning more accessible to students, teachers, and other educators.

feeds.title: Amy Brown Science
feeds.description: This blog is about a day in the life of a high school biology teacher....the triumphs, the failures, and everything in between. In the process, I would like to share teaching materials that have worked for me and my students.

feeds.title: Bright in the Middle Blog
feeds.description: I am middle school science educator with a passion for helping middle school science teachers engage their students in the classroom using research-based strategies and to make learning exciting for their students!

feeds.title: Suburban Science Blog
feeds.description: The Suburban Science blog offers teaching ideas, classroom tips, and resources for science educators, covering subjects like Anatomy, Biology, and Chemistry. It provides ideas for labs and experiments and suggests ways to boost student engagement.

feeds.title: Sunrise Science Blog
feeds.description: The Sunrise Science Classroom Blog Hey teacher friend! This blog is your go-to spot for creative ways to teach science […]

feeds.title: The Tropical Science Teacher Blog
feeds.description: The The Tropical Science Teacher blog offers resources for science teachers, with a focus on Biology and Environmental Science. The posts provide ideas for lessons, grading, and teaching tips. It features guides on creating study guides, engaging activities for teaching mitosis, and explanations of mastery grading.

feeds.title: Wild Earth Lab Blog
feeds.description: The 'Wild Earth Lab' Environmental Science Education Blog provides educational content and art related to environmental science. It features posts on a wide range of topics, including stargazing, outdoor activities, types of rocks, animal adaptations, and hands-on science experiments.

feeds.title: Science By Sinai Blog
feeds.description: Hi! My name is Karen Sinai and I am here to help you with teaching middle school science with lesson ideas, classroom management tips, planning strategies, and how to organize your science room. My goal is for you to feel comfortable in your classroom, so you can relax and enjoy your students. When you have planned well, organized yourself, strategized any potential problems, and laid out your materials, you are ready to go!

feeds.title: The Animated Teacher Blog
feeds.description: The Animated Teacher is an education blog dedicated to supporting teachers with top tips, practical pedagogy, lesson ideas and resources.

feeds.title: Elemental Science Blog
feeds.description: Sit down, grab a cup of coffee, and enjoy these teaching science tips for your homeschool, co-op, or school from our author, Paige Hudson!

feeds.title: Spectacular Science Blog
feeds.description: Spectacular Science Blog offers advice and lesson ideas for middle and high school teachers. Visit our blog feed to read our latest articles.

feeds.title: Quantum Progress
feeds.description: Raising the energy level of my physics classes. At Quantum Progress, 9th grade Atlanta physics teacher John Burk relives a childhood tradition at Physics Teacher Camp, promotes blogging as a tool for professional development, and ponders why physics buildings never win campus beauty contests.

feeds.title: Jacobs Physics
feeds.description: Resources for teachers and students of introductory physics.

feeds.title: Unifying Quantum and Relativistic Theories Blog
feeds.description: The universe's most powerful enabling tool is not knowledge or understanding but imagination because it extends the reality of one's environment.

feeds.title: Science and STEAM Team Blog
feeds.description: Hi, my name is Sarah. I have spent over 35 years in the field of elementary education. I taught special education, second grade, science, and enrichment through STEM. Currently, I am an educational curriculum designer specializing in the area of science. Our goal is to inspire teachers by making science easier to teach and to encourage students' sense of wonder!

feeds.title: Physics! ! Blog
feeds.description: Physics! Blog! shares results of The No Homework Experiment and discusses standards based grading, the goal of testing, and teaching students how to learn from mistakes.

feeds.title: The Blog of Phyz
feeds.description: High school physics education issues as seen by one California teacher: From content standards to critical thinking.

feeds.title: Chillax Science
feeds.description: Reizelie has a passion for developing science curriculum that engages children while developing in-depth scientific thinking and skills. Reizelie also loves helping teachers, schools, and homeschooling families improve their science curriculum in ways that are authentic to scientists' work.

feeds.title: Mr. Barlow's Blog - A Bunch of Interesting Stuff
feeds.description: Mr. Barlow is a high school science teacher and podcaster from Melbourne, Australia who shares interesting science studies, cool science news, and optical illusions at his blog.

feeds.title: Science teacher
feeds.description: Breaking out of the classroom into the world. A science teacher and former pediatrican finds an exemplary model in Dr. Seuss, challenges technophiles to understand deeply, and explains why he has made a tradition of culminating each school year with a field trip to watch horseshoe crabs in the throes of romance.

feeds.title: Mrs. Harris Teaches
feeds.description: Mrs.Harris Teaches is dedicated to helping science teachers in the upper elementary to high school classroom. It offers ideas, lesson plans, and activities to help students better understand science topics.

feeds.title: NGS Magnified Blog
feeds.description: Explore the variety of science teacher resources, articles, Nitty Gritty Science news, deals and more in the NGS Blog

feeds.title: Elementary Nest » Science
feeds.description: Hey, teachers! I am Jessica Tobin from Elementary Nest. In 2009, I began my journey as an elementary teacher. I first started as a kindergarten teacher, but hopped around to 1st and 2nd grade. My goal with this website is to share teaching ideas that will strengthen your teaching and provide materials that will simplify your life.

feeds.title: Physics.Teacher.Momma.
feeds.description: Hi, I'm Marianna Ruggerio. I've taught physics since 2009. I'm incredibly passionate about increasing diversity and equity in physics, as well as mentorship of preservice and novice teachers. Here you will find me sharing my classroom ideas, reflections and making Physics Education Research tangible for fellow high school teachers.

feeds.title: Science of Curiosity Blog
feeds.description: I am Jessica Parker, founder of Science of Curiosity. I started this blog to give back to the amazing teaching community that I relied on, and still go to when I need help which is often! We all need each other to be the best teacher we can be for ourselves

feeds.title: Science Teaching Junkie, Inc.
feeds.description: Addicted to Teaching with a Preference for Middle School Science.

feeds.title: Fiendishlyclever
feeds.description: A not-for-profit website dedicated to helping teachers with science and information technology advice.Rob Butler is a school leader at a special school academy, chartered teacher of science and ASE activist.

feeds.title: Get Real! Science
feeds.description: GRS is the Warner School of Education's science teacher preparation program committed to social justice through meaningful and authentic science inquiry.
